Bitcoin Searched More Than Covid-19 as it Reaches $60,000
On March 13, Bitcoin broke through the $60,000 barrier as it set a new all-time high at the milestone price. This follows on from the explosive growth to $50,000 in February. As the cryptocurrency is going more mainstream each week, it was revealed that Bitcoin is searched twice as much as Covid-19. That may come as a shock to many people but, with all the recent news, it is not actually that surprising. While Alex Jones, the notorious conspiracy theorist, reportedly lost a laptop with over $500 million worth of BTC on it, the French government is moving to auction off $34.5 million worth of Bitcoin that was seized in 2019. Many people pointed out the hypocrisy in this. The French government had previously claimed that Bitcoin is only used for criminal activity, yet they intend to sell it themselves. Meitu Inc, on the other hand, purchased 379 BTC for roughly $18 million while MicroStategy purchased another $15 million worth of Bitcoin. >>Source 1, 2, 3, 4, 5


Atari's Crypto Casino
Atari is known for playing a role in popularizing video games between 1970 and 2000. The brand was, at one point, a household name. Today, they are still rather popular, but not many children have an Atari machine on their Christmas list. Atari has revealed that, in partnership with Decentral Games, they are launching an online casino. You might assume that it would be similar to other gambling websites. Well, that is not the case. The casino will be inside Decentrland, a virtual world built on the Ethereum blockchain. For adults, the casino will be somewhat of a throwback, taking them back to some of their favorite childhood games. Players will be able use the official currency of Decentraland (MANA), DAI, and the casino's own token (ATRI). While playing, users can earn some of Decentral Games' own token. >>Source


Six Months of Summer
As more and more data is gathered researchers are finding that climate change has far more effects than many have noticed. Armed with new evidence it is clear to see the changes that have occurred to the planet’s seasons. “The new study found that, on average, summer grew from 78 to 95 days between 1952 to 2011, while winter shrank from 76 to 73 days. Spring and autumn also contracted from 124 to 115 days, and 87 to 82 days, respectively”. Animal migration and plant flowering times have also been altered. Researchers hope they’ll be able to make accurate predictions for the future using this data. >>Source

Robots on the Loose
A new study suggests that patients may be open to receiving health care from robots. Researchers are excited about this prospect as it could help reduce unnecessary contact being patients and health care professionals. “The numbers from the study suggest that it could be worthwhile to try to develop robots that can perform procedures that currently require a lot of human efforts, such as turning a patient over in bed, the researchers say”. Participants in the study also reported that the experience was no different than a traditional visit. Wait times are also expected to be decreased as more and more hospitals begin to use this technology. >>Source

Holograms Gone Wild
By this time we are no longer strangers to virtual reality, however, new breakthroughs could have major impacts on the industry. Currently, the technology we use to create virtual reality is known to have negative effects such as nausea and eye strain.“The team says the new system could help immerse VR viewers in more realistic scenery while eliminating eye strain and other side effects of long-term VR use.” Computer-generated holograms could reduce the strain, but weren’t feasible until recently when researchers realized artificial intelligence can be used to generate the holograms. This breakthrough also has the possibility of being used for a variety of purposes as well. >>Source


Edens Zero Anime's Video Reveals More Cast, T.M.Revolution Song, Netflix 2021 Streaming
A new promotional video of the anime based on the manga Edens Zero by Hiro Mashima was released on Friday by the official website of the anime. The video revealed new cast members for the anime, the new theme song of the anime and also previewed the new opening theme song  "Eden through the rough" by Takanori Nishikawa (T.M. Revolution). Netflix revealed the English-subtitled version of the video which is a hint that they will be streaming the anime sometime this year. >>Source

HIDIVE Adds Sushi Police Anime to Catalog
Sushi Police anime series was premiered in Japan on January 2016 and was streamed on the Tokyo MX station. Finally the rest of the world is getting the anime series as well! On Thursday HIDIVE announce that it will begin streaming all 13 episodes of the series (Sushi Police 3D CG) on March 18. The anime story is about a group of 3 men. The leader Honda, the data analyst Suzuki and the android inspector Kawasaki. Together they investigate restaurants in Tokyo 2020. >>Source

Crunchyroll Adds Saiyuki Reload Gunlock Anime to Catalog

2021 Crayon Shin-chan Film Reveals More Cast, Poster
New poster visual and more cast members  for the the 29th film in the Crayon Shin-chan franchise, Eiga Crayon Shin-chan Nazo Meki! Hana no Tenkasu Gakuen (Crayon Shin-chan the Movie - Shrouded in Mystery! The Flowers of Tenkazu Academy) were revealed on Tuesday by the official website of the anime.
The new cast members include:

  • Ryou Hirohashi as Chishio Azuki, the student council president who forms the Kasukabe detective club
  • Ayumu Murase as Sasuga Mamesawa, the top elite student of Tenkasu Academy
  • Tarô Yamaguchi as the headmaster of Tenkasu Academy
  • Ayaka Saito as Nororo, the president of the biology club
  • Tetsu Inada as the delinquent ringleader who divides the academy
  • Yoshiko Kamei as Shinnosuke's homeroom teacher in Tenkasu Academy
  • Rei Sakuma as Otsumun, Tenkasu Academy's AI assistant
